events.text: Your closest classmate pulls you aside after the bell and asks you to keep a secret about something that happened at home.

choices.label: Listen and keep it quiet
choices.resultText: They trust you more. At school, that kind of loyalty gets noticed.

choices.label: Tell them to talk to a teacher
choices.resultText: You push them toward help. It feels heavy, but adult, and they don't hate you for it.

choices.label: Gossip about it later
choices.resultText: Word spreads by lunch. Your reputation takes a hit with people who matter.

events.text: Your group project partner has done almost nothing. Presentation day is tomorrow and the slides are a mess.

choices.label: Stay up late and finish it yourself
choices.resultText: You carry the grade. The teacher praises the work — and somehow your partner still takes credit.

choices.label: Confront them and split the work now
choices.resultText: It's awkward, but they scramble. The project is average and fair.

choices.label: Tell the teacher the truth
choices.resultText: Staff intervene. You look responsible — and a little lonely at lunch for a week.

events.text: A teacher starts calling on you more and praising your answers. Other students notice — and not all of them smile about it.

choices.label: Lean into it and ask for extra work
choices.resultText: Your grades climb. A few classmates roll their eyes, but staff clearly respect you.

choices.label: Downplay it so you don't get targeted
choices.resultText: You keep the peace. You still learn, just with less spotlight.

choices.label: Use the attention to mock a rival
choices.resultText: You score a cheap laugh. The teacher looks disappointed, and so do people you like.

events.text: You catch your crush laughing at something you said in class. After school they linger near your locker like they might say hello.

choices.label: Walk over and talk
choices.resultText: It's awkward for thirty seconds, then easy. School feels brighter the rest of the week.

choices.label: Smile and keep walking
choices.resultText: Safe. Also unfinished. You replay the moment all evening.

choices.label: Panic and hide behind friends
choices.resultText: Your friends tease you for days. The crush probably didn't even notice — you hope.

events.text: The school bully corners you between buildings and demands your lunch money — or worse, your dignity in front of a crowd.

choices.label: Stand your ground
choices.resultText: It gets rough, but people stop laughing. Word spreads that you don't fold.

choices.label: Walk away and tell staff
choices.resultText: Adults finally get involved. Detention for them; quiet respect for you.

choices.label: Hand over what they want
choices.resultText: It's over quickly. The shame lasts longer than the cash.

events.text: Someone starts a rumor that you got detention for cheating — even if you didn't. The hallway chatter is loud.

choices.label: Ignore it and keep your grades clean
choices.resultText: The rumor dies without fuel. Your next test score does the talking.

choices.label: Confront the rumor-starter
choices.resultText: It gets heated. Some people believe you more; some just enjoy the drama.

choices.label: Lean into the bad-kid image
choices.resultText: You get a few laughs and lose a little staff goodwill. Reputation is a strange currency.

events.text: Your school club has a showcase night. Parents, teachers, and half the student body will be watching.

choices.label: Practice hard and take a lead role
choices.resultText: You shine. A teacher suggests you keep going with this outside school.

choices.label: Help backstage and support the team
choices.resultText: Nobody cheers your name, but the club runs smoothly because of you.

choices.label: Skip it and hang out elsewhere
choices.resultText: You miss the night. The group notices — and so does your club advisor.

events.text: Exam week hits like a wall. Everyone is tired, caffeinated, and one bad night away from melting down.

choices.label: Build a study schedule and stick to it
choices.resultText: Boring works. You walk into the hall knowing the material.

choices.label: Cram with friends overnight
choices.resultText: You learn some things and forget others. Bonding helps the stress, not the sleep.

choices.label: Give up and wing it
choices.resultText: Freedom feels good until the first question. Then it doesn't.

events.text: A transfer student sits alone at lunch looking lost. A few people stare; nobody moves.

choices.label: Invite them to sit with you
choices.resultText: They smile like they haven't in weeks. School gets a little bigger for both of you.

choices.label: Point them toward a teacher
choices.resultText: Helpful, distant. You did something — just not the hard part.

choices.label: Pretend you didn't notice
choices.resultText: You eat in peace. The quiet still feels wrong.

events.text: A professor's office hours are open. Your assignment is confusing and the lecture notes don't fill the gap.

choices.label: Go and ask focused questions
choices.resultText: They clarify the hard part in ten minutes. You leave feeling like a real student.

choices.label: Email a vague cry for help
choices.resultText: You get a polite reply pointing back to the syllabus. Progress: minimal.

choices.label: Skip it and copy from a friend
choices.resultText: You submit something. Understanding it is a problem for future-you.
